dataIdInfo.idPurp: Schema-aware geoprocessing tasks for identifying features near user-supplied reference features.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
Find Features Near Features

A synchronous geoprocessing tool that returns input features within a specified geodesic distance of reference features.

How It Works

The tool optionally filters the input and reference layers, then selects input features within the supplied distance of the reference features. For count questions, use the selected_feature_count result. Do not count the returned feature geometry.

Parameters

  • Input Features: The features to evaluate. For REST requests, supply a FeatureServer layer URL: https://.../FeatureServer/0.
  • Input Features Where Clause: Optional SQL filter for the input features.
  • Proximity Features: The reference features. For REST requests, supply a FeatureServer layer URL: https://.../FeatureServer/0.
  • Proximity Features Where Clause: Optional SQL filter for the reference features.
  • Search Distance: A linear distance such as 10 Meters.
  • Output Features: Features from the input layer that meet the proximity condition.
  • Selected Feature Count: The number of selected input features. Use this derived result to answer count questions.

SQL Filter Requirements

Before supplying either SQL where clause, inspect the schema of the selected feature layer. Use the layer's physical field names and verified attribute values; do not use display aliases as SQL field names. The expression must use SQL syntax supported by the referenced feature service.

For example, use FIELD_NAME = 'verified value' only after confirming that both the field and value exist in the selected layer. Leave a where clause blank to include all features from that layer.

Example Workflow

  1. Select the layer to evaluate as Input Features.
  2. Optionally filter the input layer with a verified SQL expression.
  3. Select the reference layer as Proximity Features.
  4. Optionally filter the reference layer with a verified SQL expression.
  5. Set Search Distance to the required linear distance.
  6. Use selected_feature_count to answer a count question.

Notes

  • The tool uses geodesic distance.
  • Both layers should have compatible spatial references for accurate distance analysis.
  • An invalid SQL expression prevents the tool from running; validate field names and values against the selected layer before execution.
